title: Brahmaputra Infrastructure Ltd - 535693 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 50% to INR365 crore and PAT nearly doubled to INR59.61 crore, with an INR1,600 crore order book (4.46x FY26 revenue).
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) revenue from operations of INR365 crore, up 50% from INR242 crore, with EBITDA of INR83.45 crore (margin 22.83%, up 280 bps) and PAT of INR59.61 crore (up roughly 100%). Management attributed the gain to Q2 and Q3 monsoon-quarter execution, where revenue reached INR180 crore versus INR70 crore a year earlier. Q4 standalone revenue was INR93.93 crore, PBT INR16.79 crore, PAT INR14.78 crore and EPS INR5.09. This was the company's first earnings call, and Q&A covered order book conversion, real estate plans, promoter pledge, and JV revenue sharing.

financial_highlights.change: PBT INR16.79 crore; YoY not stated

segments.name: EPC infrastructure
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR349.81 crore (roughly 90% of total) with segment profit INR51.88 crore. Management said EPC margins range 13-20%, averaging about 15%, with niche river and slope protection works at 18-19%.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: Revenue INR19.58 crore (about 5-7% of total per an analyst's figure; management said about 10%), with segment profit INR16.70 crore vs INR14.75 crore last year. Revenue fell because FY25 included industrial plot sales (about INR4 crore) that did not recur. Management cited about 85% margins, almost entirely rental.

segments.name: Order book by vertical
segments.commentary: Total INR1,600 crore: Roads and Bridges INR498 crore, Buildings INR405 crore, Railways and Tunnels INR400 crore, River Protection INR250 crore. About 60% expected to execute in FY27 and 40% to spill into FY28.

guidance_outlook: Management targets maintaining about 50% revenue growth and current profitability margins over the next two to three years, and said it expects this momentum for about five years.
Bidding pipeline of about INR3,000 crore with results expected in 30-45 days; full-year FY27 pipeline expected at INR7,000-8,000 crore.

New phased retail/plaza project in Guwahati, about INR500 crore total value over four to five years, about 4 lakh sq ft CLA, launch expected in four to five months; management expects a visible jump in real estate revenue by year-end.
Management cited a target of about INR60 crore rental income by FY29/FY30 (question wording varied); phased leasable-area growth was described as the route.
Projects expected to be about 70% BIL and 30% JV partners by revenue, varying project to project.
capex_capacity: Funding for new projects planned through surety bonds (now accepted across all departments), bank guarantees, and joint ventures; no capex or capacity figures were given.
Near-continuous execution achieved in the monsoon quarters by shifting workflow to lower-rainfall areas; no capacity utilisation numbers disclosed.
Average execution period for new bids is two to three years.
demand_pricing: Order book of INR1,600 crore at FY26 end, 4.46x FY26 revenue; about 50% acquired in the last six months, and management said revenue recognition from new orders takes six to seven months due to design and land work.
Pipeline mix stated as about 40% buildings, 20% protection works and 40% roads.

Management cited Northeast drivers: PM Gati Shakti, Bharatmala, Act East, five to six railway lines in 10 years, Bhutan (Gelephu) rail bid, border roads and fencing, hydropower in Arunachal, and district-level universities and hospitals in Assam.
Management said Northeast competitors are fewer, and that NE projects (terrain, river and slope protection) carry higher margins than mainland contractors.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR1,600 crore order book is executable in FY27 versus FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% is expected to execute in FY27 and 40% to spill into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are road projects on HAM and what are segmental margins?
qa_highlights.answer: All road projects are EPC or item-rate; none are HAM. EPC margins range 13-20%, averaging about 15%, with niche works at 18-19% and general infrastructure at 11-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is promoter pledge high despite lower debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Shares were pledged in 2014 when debt was higher; management is negotiating release with lenders and hopes to release it within one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book not show up in Q4 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 50% of the book was won in the last six months; EPC design, land and approvals take six to seven months before revenue recognition begins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bid pipeline and FY27 bidding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Current pipeline is about INR3,000 crore with results in 30-45 days; FY27 bidding is expected at INR7,000-8,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did real estate revenue fall in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included about INR4 crore of industrial plot sales that did not recur in FY26; real estate profit rose to INR16.70 crore from INR14.75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be deployed to fund growth, and is there a debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to surety bonds plus bank guarantees, and JVs with partners, rather than a stated debt reduction target.

qa_highlights.question: What share of order book revenue goes to JV partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approximately 70% of order book revenue comes to BIL and 30% to JV partners, varying by project.

risks_watch: Promoter share pledge remains high; release depends on lender consultations with no firm timeline beyond one to two years.
Q4 revenue of INR93.93 crore and FY26 growth depend on a single monsoon-season execution shift; sustainability of Q2/Q3 gains is unproven.
Real estate revenue growth hinges on the new Guwahati project launch in four to five months, which is still in planning and not yet approved.
Conversion of the INR3,000 crore pipeline in 30-45 days, and the FY27 target of INR7,000-8,000 crore bidding, are unverified.
Revenue share of JV partners (about 30%) reduces BIL's consolidated take; the standalone-consolidated split was stated inconsistently on the call.
Disclosure inconsistencies: real estate share of revenue was given as about 10% by management and 5-7% by an analyst; PAT and EPS were mixed between standalone and consolidated figures.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and Northeast positioning, with specific figures on order book and margins. Cautious or vague on pledge release timing, debt reduction and the real estate pipeline, which had no capex or cost figures.
key_quotes: So, our target is to maintain the same growth percentage and ensure that we are able to maintain the same rate of profitability as well.
So, we see this as an inflection point for a better future.
EPC will definitely be the revenue driver because it is a lot more scalable.
